name: Chiribiquete Emerald
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia (sierra de chiribiquete)
description: Poorly known hummingbird found only in the remote Chiribiquete Mountains in southeastern Colombia, far from the Andes. Male is iridescent green with a bluish tail.

name: Northern Black-throated Trogon
rangeDescription: Northern honduras to far northwestern colombia
description: Yellow-bellied trogon with pale blue eyering and yellowish bill. Male has shimmering green-blue upperparts and chest; female is brown.

name: Fan-tailed Warbler
rangeDescription: Tropical western mexico (southeastern sonora) to north-central nicaragua
description: Attractive, rather large warbler with long, expressive, white-tipped tail. Occurs in tropical forest of foothills and lowlands, mainly in winter, especially in areas with open understory and boulders.

name: Snow Mountain Robin
rangeDescription: New guinea (mount wilhelmina and mount carstensz)
description: A fairly small, localised bird of bare, rocky slopes above the treeline on certain peaks in the Snow Mountains. Overall sooty grey color, paler on the sides and belly, a narrow white band on the forehead and a large red patch on the chest.

name: Long-winged Harrier
rangeDescription: Grassland of tropical south america, including trinidad and tobago
description: Striking, long-tailed and long-winged harrier. Glides with wings held in a raised v-shape.

name: Ward's Trogon
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern china (yunnan), eastern bhutan, northern myanmar, and northwestern vietnam
description: A sluggish bird of mature tropical hill forests. A small head and prominent pale eye-ring give it a comically surprised appearance.

name: Purple-winged Roller
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including lembeh, bangka, and manterawu (off northeast), and muna and buton islands (off southeast)
description: A distinctive big-billed bird that is entirely deep purple in color except for a conspicuous sky-blue cap and rump. Juvenile has a duller cap and browner underparts.

name: Black-headed Bunting
rangeDescription: South-central eurasia; winters to india
description: Large, stocky bunting. On breeding males, the combination of a black head, a bright yellow collar, yellow underparts, and rusty-brown back is unmistakable.

name: Samoan Starling
rangeDescription: Samoa and american samoa
description: A large starling with a long tail and a strong bill. Body and wings dull brown.

name: White-browed Crake
rangeDescription: Southern thailand, indochina, and philippines to coastal northern australia and southwestern oceania
description: A delicate-looking inhabitant of densely vegetated wetlands, where it scrambles over floating plants and between the stems of standing ones. Brown above and pale gray below, with a small black mask around the eye bound in by two bold white stripes.

name: Cape Griffon
rangeDescription: Open plains and mountains of southern africa
description: Overall the Cape Griffon is creamy-white, much paler and larger than the White-backed Vulture. At close range, the adult’s eyes are honey-colored, and there is a speckled stripe along the middle of the wing.

name: Caspian Tern
rangeDescription: Breeds patchily coastal baltic sea and inland southeast europe to western mongolia and ussuriland (southeastern russia) and northeastern china and southern asian coasts; coastal and inland western and southern africa; europa (west of southern madagascar, mozambique channel), coastal madagascar and aldabra group (southwestern seychelles); coastal and inland northern and eastern australia, coastal new zealand (north, south and stewart islands); inland northwest territories to northeastern canada, in south to central california and great lakes; winters to coastal africa, red sea, persian gulf, india, thailand, malay peninsula, and vietnam; eastern pacific and caribbean to panama
description: Largest tern in the world; widespread but typically uncommon. Thick, bright-red bill is distinctive; most have small dark marking near the tip.

name: Djibouti Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Montane forest of forêt du day (djibouti)
description: Attractive francolin that is critically endangered and confined to a corner of Djibouti. The back is gray and the neck and underparts are heavily marked with rufous and gray.

name: Wonga Pigeon
rangeDescription: Coastal forest of eastern australia (central queensland to southeastern victoria)
description: Large rainforest pigeon, often found foraging on the ground on stocky pink legs. From behind it presents as a steel-gray bird with uniformly gray wings, back and tail.

name: Streamer-tailed Tyrant
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to paraguay, south-central and southeastern brazil, and northeastern argentina
description: Spectacular flycatcher with a long and deeply forked tail. Grayish overall with a white throat and a black half collar that is continuous with the eye stripe.

name: Slate-colored Hawk
rangeDescription: Tropical southern venezuela to eastern bolivia and amazonian brazil
description: Chunky, broad-winged slate gray hawk with white tail bands and bright red facial skin, bill, and legs. Closely associated with water, and most frequently found in singles and pairs perched around oxbow lakes, forested streams, flooded forests, and floodplain forests.

name: Bismarck Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Lowlands of bismarck archipelago
description: A medium-sized blue-and-white kingfisher with a big, heavy black bill. Bluish-green upperparts and chest band contrast with creamy white underparts and white neck patch.

name: Atlas Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Morocco (south to middle atlas mountains), northern algeria, and northern tunisia
description: Very similar and closely related to European Pied Flycatcher. Males have mixed features of Collared and European Pied Flycatchers, but note very large white wing patch and big white forehead.

name: Ochre-flanked Tapaculo
rangeDescription: South-central chile (santiago to chiloé) and adjacent argentina; mocha island
description: Heard but rarely seen; a retiring little gray bird of bamboo thickets and other dense shrubbery at forest edges, along streams, and in wooded patches. Can be confiding if an observer is quiet.

name: Acadian Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Breeds eastern usa; winters nicaragua to ecuador and venezuela
description: Small flycatcher with big peaked head and relatively long bill. Extremely similar to several other species, especially Alder and Willow Flycatchers.
